extracted.intended_audience: writers entering the NYCMidnight 250-word Microfiction Challenge / microfiction competition participants
extracted.subtask_description: Produce and submit an original 250-word microfiction for the NYCMidnight competition following the contest's assignments (genre, action, word), timing, and submission rules. Compete within a randomly assigned group through multiple 48-hour rounds for advancement and prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 250-word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Create very short stories no longer than 250 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition imposes a strict word limit — stories must be 250 words or fewer. Participant testimonials emphasize that the tight word count forces compression and discipline in craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned genre, action, and word
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers are assigned a genre, action, and word assignment for each round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must craft your story in the assigned genre, have the assigned action take place in the story, and incorporate the assigned word. These three elements are mandatory components of the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 48-hour creation window
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have 48 hours to craft an original 250-word story after assignments are released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rounds begin at specified times (e.g., 11:59 PM New York time for kickoff). Use the countdown clock and upload by the submission deadline for that 48-hour period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / created during competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted stories must be original works created for the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly refers to 'original 250-word story' and implies submissions should be new material produced within the round's time window. Writers retain rights but entries are expected to be original to the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random group placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers are placed randomly in groups for judging and advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition structure pairs writers into groups; judges pick top stories within each group to advance. Your competition peers are the other members of your assigned group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement: top 10 advance from Round 1
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 1st Round, judges choose a top 10 in each group to advance to the 2nd Round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection from each group is judge-driven; meeting the assignment and standing out among your group are necessary to be among the top 10 who advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement: top 5 advance from Round 2 to Final
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 2nd Round, judges select the top 5 writers in each group to advance to the Final Round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again, judges' selections determine advancement; Final Round entrants receive a final assignment and have the same 48-hour timeframe to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges provide feedback for every submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback from the judges is provided for every submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every entrant receives judge feedback on their submission. The page highlights feedback as a key benefit of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review forum availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A special review forum is available for participants to submit stories for review from fellow writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers are encouraged to use the community forum to get peer feedback throughout the competition; the organizers describe the forum as welcoming and helpful for all levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of rights / publication consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers retain all the rights to the stories they create during the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organizers state they 'could not and would not share the stories publicly without consent from the authors.' Authors therefore retain control over publication or public sharing of their entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission/upload instructions and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be uploaded according to the contest's submission instructions and by the round deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to specific upload instructions and includes countdown clocks for submission windows; it warns that emails may go to spam and recommends marking calendars and using 'Add to Calendar' to avoid missing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare with recommended microfiction resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers recommend reading provided tips and blog posts on microfiction craft before competing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured resources include 'Anatomy of Microfiction', 'Five strategies to craft tiny stories', interviews with past winners, and posts on plot twists, character arc, and structuring beginning/middle/end in microfiction — useful preparatory material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes and incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: There are thousands in cash and prizes for winners (e.g., $4,500 to first place).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full prize list is available via a link. The page also offers promotional discounts (e.g., $5 off entry fee for social-posting) and notes that part of entry fees are donated to charities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charitable donation from entry fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Two percent from each entry fee will be donated to listed charities, and writers can choose where their donation goes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a contest policy tied to entry fees; entrants should be aware that donations are part of the fee structure and may be able to designate recipients.
